transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-02
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Sana Patel (Redwood SE), Alex Rivera (Atlas CTO), Priya Desai (Lead ML Eng), Marco Li (Infra)

Summary: quick discovery focused on time-to-first-token (TTFT) for PLG/self-serve, free credits allocation, and decision criteria between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem). Heavy emphasis on data residency, KMS, and perf targets. Agreed to run a light perf test with a small dataset and reconvene next week.

Topics: credits and onboarding, hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs, SSO/KMS requirements, expected QPS and latency SLOs, security docs and SOC2, next steps and owners.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (AE): hey everyone thanks for carving out time today, can we do quick intros?
[00:06] Alex (CTO): yeah hi i'm alex, i'm cto at atlas cartography, we do large-scale map annotations and vector tiling, priya and marco are with me.
[00:12] Priya (ML): hi all, priya, i lead the ml team, mostly model infra and productionization.
[00:15] Marco (Infra): marco here, infra eng, focus on networking and on-prem gateways.
[00:18] Jordan (AE): perfect, and from redwood, sana is our se, she'll cover perf and the private path, i'm the AE so i'll cover credits/pricing and onboarding. quick goal for today: understand your constraints and map to hosted/dedicated/private, and get you to first token as fast as possible. sound right?
[00:33] Alex (CTO): yep that's it, timeline is pretty tight — stakeholder ask is proof of concept in two weeks, then internal review.
[00:39] Sana (SE): great — can you share a bit about expected QPS, payload sizes, and any PII concerns?
[00:44] Priya (ML): payloads are small, mostly telemetry+metadata, avg 220 tokens per request. QPS target for proof is 15-20 synched requests per second, bursty up to 50. we care about tail latency under 300ms for 90th perc. data residency: all inference must stay in-eu for this POC.
[00:59] Marco (Infra): and encryption at rest with our KMS is required if we do any private deployment.
[01:05] Jordan (AE): okay that's helpful. for PLG/self-serve hosted -> we can allocate credits and you can onboard right away, region selection includes eu-west and frankfurt regions which satisfy residency.
[01:15] Alex (CTO): fair, what's the TTFT for someone using the hosted flow — from signup to first token?
[01:20] Jordan (AE): generally under an hour for straightforward use-cases — sign-up, apply credits, API key, sample curl or SDK request. but to hit your perf and tail latency goals you'd want to run a quick perf job, which usually takes a day to tune batch sizes and model variants.
[01:34] Priya (ML): quick question: our model size is around 13B, do you host open models or do we bring our own?
[01:40] Sana (SE): we host curated open models and also support private model artifacts if you want; for hosted we have verified 13B quantized builds that optimize latency. for dedicated you can reserve capacity and pin a model build; for private on-prem you bring your own image or we deploy a customer-managed runtime.
[01:52] Marco (Infra): if we go private, how heavy is the on-prem install? we are air-gapped in parts of our infra.
[01:57] Sana (SE): private installers support an air-gapped mode — it's a bit more involved: need host access, some kernel modules, and storage for model shards. typical on-prem bootstrap is 2-3 days plus config; for a quicker POC we often do VPC deployment into customer cloud region which meets residency and is faster.
[02:14] Alex (CTO): so for the two-week POC, hosted eu-region sounds fastest. can we still encrypt with our KMS?
[02:20] Jordan (AE): yes — hosted supports per-customer encryption keys via KMS integration for enterprise tiers, and for Dedicated/Private it's straightforward to use your KMS/HSM. i'll flag that we may need an enterprise ent to enable KMS on hosted; we'll scope it.
[02:33] Priya (ML): pricing — how do credits map to expected token consumption? we want a rough calc for the POC.
[02:38] Jordan (AE): baseline: generation tokens billed per output token, and embeddings per request; i'll send a tailored estimate but for your workload (220 tokens avg, 15 QPS sustained) rough math: 15 qps * 220 tokens * 3600 sec * t = many tokens — but for a two-week POC we usually allocate a mid-tier credit pack that covers ~5M tokens. we'll include a projection in the email.
[02:58] Marco (Infra): are there rate limits or shared noisy neighbors on hosted?
[03:02] Sana (SE): hosted will have rate limits on free tiers; for paid customers we can raise rate limits and for Dedicated it's isolated capacity so no noisy neighbors. we also support burst policies on Dedicated for traffic spikes.
[03:15] Alex (CTO): what about function/tool calling and streaming? we need streaming for progressive responses to our UI.
[03:21] Sana (SE): streaming is supported on hosted and Dedicated; private supports it too but may need extra network tweaks. small caveat: streaming latency is impacted by batch windows, we can tune it.
[03:34] Jordan (AE): any compliance or security docs you need now? we can share SOC2, ISO, and our security pack.
[03:40] Alex (CTO): yes please, and also a list of what logs are retained and for how long — our legal team will ask.
[03:45] Jordan (AE): noted — i'll include retention details. we also support per-token tracing and you can disable persist if needed.
[03:50] Priya (ML): if we test with your hosted 13B quantized model, what's the expected 90th perc latency at 15 qps?
[03:57] Sana (SE): ballpark on an optimized build in eu region: 90th under 200-250ms for single-token stream? hmm, single request of 220 tokens the per-token latency is low but total generation time will depend on tokens produced — often total resp time for 220 tokens could be 600-800ms depending on model and batching. to hit 300ms total we'd look at a smaller model variant or aggressive quant/comp settings or Dedicated with tuned kernels.
[04:22] Alex (CTO): got it. so it's tradeoff: hosted faster to start but may need dedicated for stricter SLOs.
[04:27] Jordan (AE): exactly. for your POC we recommend hosted eu with credits, run perf, then if tails are too high we propose a Dedicated trial or a VPC Private pilot.
[04:36] Marco (Infra): what's the onboarding experience for our infra folks? can we SSO into console?
[04:40] Jordan (AE): yes SSO via SAML/Okta is supported on paid accounts. console roles, RBAC, audit logs are available.
[04:48] Priya (ML): what's footprint for dedicated? we want rough GPU counts for 13B at 20 qps.
[04:53] Sana (SE): rough guide: a single A100/80GB equivalent can handle ~20-30 rps depending on batch and kv cache usage for 13B. for predictable throughput we'd size a small pool of 2-3 devices with autoscale. i'll send an estimated capacity plan based on your qps.
[05:08] Alex (CTO): competition: we've been talking to a couple onprem vendors and lambda labs, they pitch lower unit cost but more ops. how do you compare?
[05:16] Jordan (AE): we focus on predictability and developer experience — less ops for you, clear metrics on cost/latency, and unified path to private if needed. i'll include a short comparison doc.
[05:25] Marco (Infra): one blocker could be our compliance team wanting audit proof for electron logs — do you expose raw request IDs and timestamps?
[05:33] Sana (SE): yes audit logs include request IDs, timestamps, route, model version — we can redact prompt content on request.
[05:40] Alex (CTO): ok next step: priya will share a 1000-row sample of anonymized requests and we want a perf run.
[05:47] Priya (ML): yes i'll prepare a small slice and ping you.
[05:50] Jordan (AE): timeline: i'll allocate quickstart credits today — you'll get an email with signup and a 7-day elevated quota; sana will run the perf with the dataset and share numbers in a 48-hour run. we'll then schedule a follow-up to review and decide hosted vs dedicated pilot.
[06:05] Marco (Infra): good. also we need to validate KMS flow; if we can do that in hosted that would accelerate approvals.
[06:12] Sana (SE): we can demo KMS flow in hosted but full enterprise keying often requires a short contract. for the POC we can do a pseudo-KMS flow or demonstrate key wrap. i'll detail options.
[06:24] Alex (CTO): great. one more — do you provide a checklist for private deploy prerequisites? we might need to show the security team.
[06:30] Sana (SE): yes there's a private deployment checklist — i'll attach it. includes network ports, storage, minimum kernel versions, and artifact signing.
[06:38] Jordan (AE): cool, let's recap. next steps: jordan send credits + signup + pricing; sana share perf runbook + checklist + perf estimate; priya send data slice; we reconvene after perf (target next thursday).
[06:52] Alex (CTO): sounds good, thanks everyone.
[06:55] Jordan (AE): thanks, we'll follow up via email, i'll cc legal and security doc links.
[06:59] End of meeting.

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcription had a few mis-attributed speaker labels and some technical terms like 'kv cache' appeared as 'kay vee cache' in places.
